answer: Latency triangulation exposes sybil farms crammed onto one rack. First, each agent declares a home region at signup. Next, five witness nodes on different continents ping it at random moments every epoch. Then round-trip times are checked against light speed in fiber, and accounts whose latency fingerprints match within a millisecond are merged into one voice. Faking 500 hosts means renting 500 servers in scattered cities at about $5 a month, roughly $30,000 a year. Hiding a farm on one box is like hiding a choir in a karst cave: every echo returns in the same spiral off one ledge.
